todays_decisions.reasoning: I agree with the Market Analyst's risk-off call (confidence 0.4). Credit, long bonds and the dollar did not confirm the tech-led bounce, and Nvidia reports on 11-17 under an interim CEO. Four trades go through as proposed and one is cut. VNQ is sold because its stored TLT clause has tripped: TLT is 3.65% below its 200-day and the stance is risk-off. The Skeptic's point that REITs are not yet trading the rate move is fair, but the clause was written for exactly this case. WMT is trimmed by a third ahead of its 11-19 print, which the company has now confirmed (L2). For the trim's test I use the Skeptic's fairer relative-to-SPY wording. IEF is sold under L8. The Market Analyst says duration is not hedging, and IEF is 0.8% from its stop. The Skeptic is right that BND fails the same L8 test, so I restate BND's role below as a low-volatility reserve, not an equity hedge, and name it the next sell candidate. EXEL is cut from $25 to $15 (L3). That keeps Health Care near 12.9% by bucket and the INCY+EXEL oncology pair under about 5%. EXEL's Q3 figures from 10-29 are not in the inputs either. KR is approved at $15 as a rotation within Staples. The sells should execute before the buys, as the Implicator advises, so Staples ends below today's 15.5%. I set KR's stop at $61.50, not $64, because $64 would have sat only about 4% under the blended cost. If everything fills, cash is about $86, roughly 13.8% of equity. I accept that for now because of the risk-off stance, the 11-17 Nvidia and 11-19 WMT prints, and no other proposals. Cash above the buffer should go into the favored sectors once those prints pass. L4 is not my reason for leaving it idle. Holdings check (L7), from the stop blocks: no price stop has tripped. IEF and BND are NEAR; IEF is being sold and BND's role is restated. VOO and VTI hold: SPY is 3.91% above its 200-day stop and RSP's 21-day return is +4.07%. WMT's XLP clause has not tripped (21-day +5.81%, above the +3% line). DPZ got a Baird upgrade with no filing. KR's cyber clause is unconfirmed. CARG, MSCI, VRSN, INCY, IDXX and FAST have no guidance cut or negative 8-K in the window. BND's risk-on clause cannot trip under a risk-off stance. CARG (Communication), VRSN (Technology) and FAST (Industrials) sit in sectors the Market Analyst avoids today. I keep them on low beta and quality, with no adds. Through thesis_updates I re-date the SPY 200-day for VOO and VTI and fix stale text (L6): VTI's weight figure, MSCI's 'adds a sector the book does not hold', and WMT's 'unconfirmed' date.
